children: Nomura has retained its 'Buy' rating on Sun Pharmaceutical Industries but cut its target price to Rs 2,260 from Rs 2,400, citing a slowdown in its specialty business despite strong growth in India. The brokerage expects specialty growth to recover in FY28 and FY29 and remains constructive on the company's proposed acquisition of Organon.

Sun Pharma's Q2FY27 performance came in ahead of Nomura's estimates, with revenue and EBITDA beating its forecasts by 1% and 8%, respectively. Adjusted net profit rose 4% year-on-year to Rs 32.5 billion and was 10% above the brokerage's estimate.

Growth was in double digits across all key segments except the US, helped partly by favourable currency movements. India revenue increased 17.3% year-on-year, with volume growth of around 6%, compared with 1.6% for the Indian Pharmaceutical Market (IPM).

US sales stood at $455 million, up $28 million sequentially from a seasonally weak base and supported by Levulan and five new generic launches. However, revenue was flat year-on-year as competition in lenalidomide and slower specialty growth offset these gains.

Global innovative medicines, or specialty, sales rose 6.9% year-on-year to $356 million. Management attributed the slowdown to Ilumya in the US. Nomura said interventions are in place and the recently approved indication for psoriatic arthritis should support a gradual recovery.
Gross margin expanded 147 basis points year-on-year to 80.8%, aided by a richer branded-generic mix and favourable currency movements.

However, EBITDA margin expansion was limited to 43 basis points, taking it to 28.4%, as selling, general and administrative expenses rose due to spending on specialty launches. Research and development expenses stood at 4.8% of sales, below the company's guidance of 6-7%.

Organon reported revenue of $1.57 billion for the third quarter of calendar year 2026, down 2% year-on-year but up 1% sequentially. Growth in biosimilars, which rose 12%, was partly offset by a 10% decline in women's health, while established brands remained flat.

Nexplanon revenue declined 10% year-on-year due to reinsertion delays and uncertainty around US federal funding. Organon's EBITDA fell 3% year-on-year to $502 million, although it increased 9% sequentially. Management expects the acquisition by Sun Pharma to be completed by the fourth quarter of FY27.

Nomura remains constructive on the transaction and expects Sun Pharma to realise $500 million in synergies, compared with the guided $350 million. Its valuation adds Rs 250 per share for Organon, based on an enterprise value-to-EBITDA multiple of 8 times.
Target price cut on lower valuation multiple

Nomura has raised its FY27 EBITDA estimate by around 4%, but cut its net profit estimate by 6% due to an exceptional charge and a higher effective tax rate. Its FY28 and FY29 estimates are broadly unchanged, with a 1% increase.

The brokerage now values Sun Pharma at 28 times its FY29 estimated earnings per share of Rs 71.9, down from 32.5 times earlier. The reduction reflects a higher cost of capital, the valuation roll-forward and multiple compression for domestic formulations amid the specialty business slowdown.
This translates into a value of Rs 2,013 per share for the base business, with an additional Rs 250 per share attributed to Organon, taking the target price to Rs 2,260.

Nomura expects specialty growth to improve in FY28 and FY29, supported by Ilumya and new launches. It also sees strong valuation support from Sun Pharma's domestic formulations and branded-generic businesses. Excluding the Organon valuation, the stock trades at 29 times and 25 times its FY28 and FY29 estimated EPS of Rs 60.9 and Rs 71.9, respectively.

title: Sun Pharma: Nomura retains 'Buy', cuts target price to Rs 2,260 after specialty business slowdown
